answer: Threshold issuance of age credentials lets a quorum of verifiers jointly certify that an applicant is over a required age, and the wharf of the design is that no verifier learns the applicant's exact birthdate. The copper of the protocol is that each verifier checks a different piece of evidence, so a single corrupt verifier cannot issue a credential alone. A Sybil cannot mint age credentials for fake accounts because issuance needs a threshold, and the reef of the credential reveals only that the age condition holds.
